newsitem.title: USA: CBOT seeks new vendor for cash Treasury brokerage.
newsitem.headline: CBOT seeks new vendor for cash Treasury brokerage.

text.p: The Chicago Board of Trade is looking for an electronic vendor for its planned government securities trading system after Liberty Brokerage Investment Corp pulled out of the venture, CBOT officials said Thursday.
"We are proceeding in a search for a vendor that will provide the electronic trading system," said an official at the exchange who requested anonymity.

At a midyear address to the exchange membership last week, CBOT Chairman Patrick Arbor said the exchange was in talks with Dow Jones & Co regarding opportunities in the area of technology and quote distribution.
The CBOT earlier this month won rights from Dow Jones to introduce futures and futures-options based on Dow indexes including the Dow 30 industrials.
CBOT officials Thursday would not comment on potential technology partners for its planned electronic system for trading cash government securities, called Chicago Board Brokerage (CBB).
Dow Jones spokesman Richard Tofel also declined to comment on whether the company was in talks with CBOT regarding the CBB project.
CBOT directors at a board meeting late Wednesday approved a restructuring of CBB that gives Prebon Yamane (USA) Inc a 40 percent equity interest in CBB.

Liberty Brokerage, which previously agreed to share a 49 percent stake in CBB with Prebon Yamane, has withdrawn from the three-way venture due to clashing business strategies, a source at Liberty said Thursday.
Liberty, Prebon and the CBOT announced in December they had formed an alliance to operate CBB, which the CBOT began developing in 1992.
CBB would permit electronic trading and clearing of a wide variety of cash government securities and over-the-counter derivatives.

"As the deal progressed, there were certain restrictions that were looked to be placed that just didn't fit with our business plan," said the Liberty source, who asked not to be named. "Our business plan and the Chicago Board of Trade's business plan diverged."

CBOT Senior Vice President Fred Grede said the arrangement between the two would-be partners fell apart over details in protracted contract negotiations, but said the exchange retains a cordial relationship with Liberty.
Neither Grede nor the Liberty source would elaborate further on what caused the falling out.
The Liberty source said the firm would proceed independently to develop an electronic system for trading over-the-counter government securities.
"We still plan to pursue an electronic platform for execution of U.S. governments," the Liberty source said.

Upon closing of the joint venture agreement with Prebon, the CBOT said Ceres Trading Limited Partnership would immediately purchase the exchange's remaining 60 percent interest in CBB. The Ceres partnership, comprising CBOT members, governs the Project A after-hours electronic trading system for exchange products.
